signals.text: Our commitment to inclusion means we actively ensure that all pupils, including those with special educational needs and disabilities, are visible, heard, represented and valued across the curriculum, within our resources, classroom environments and teaching practices.
The school has identified 49 pupils as having special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), including dyslexia and attention deficit disorder, all of whom receive additional help.

Senior Deputy Head | Elizabeth Sieczko Working at Feltonfleet comes with a host of benefits, including a generous pension scheme, discounted school fees, on-site parking, complimentary lunches during term time, and access to our swimming pool.

Head of Learning Enrichment | Fiona Houston While the number of pupils with diagnosed special educational needs at Feltonfleet is relatively small, those pupils who do require additional support benefit from regular, specialist assistance, either individually, in a small group or in their regular class.
Throughout the school, pupils of all abilities, including those with SEND and EAL, attain high standards and make excellent progress in their learning.

EDUCATION WITH PURPOSE
Exciting News
Little Doves - Year Round Nursery
This is Feltonfleet -
where individuals really matter
At Feltonfleet School, our core values of honesty, respect, responsibilty, and kindness guide every step of our journey, fostering a nurturing environment where each student can thrive and succeed.
"At Feltonfleet, honesty means telling the truth and being honest with myself. It’s about making a place where everyone can be honest too, and always acting truthfully. Being honest helps us be open, see things clearly, and understand better. At school, I've learned that being my truthful self is the best way to be."
"Feltonfleet has taught me that responsibility means taking ownership of my actions and doing what I’m supposed to do, even when it's hard. It’s about being reliable, helping others, and making good choices so I can be trusted. Responsibility helps us become better people and build a stronger community."
"Respect at Feltonfleet means being nice to everyone and treating them like they matter. We learn to make good choices that help us get along with others, even if they're different. Respect helps us all feel important and valued."

Senior School Destinations
Each year, 100% of Feltonfleet pupils secure places at first-rate senior schools and, on average, one in three pupils wins a senior school scholarship in recognition of their particular talents in a specific discipline.

Feltonfleet’s aim is not only to prepare pupils for academic success but also to be mentally agile and emotionally robust.
Location
Feltonfleet's 25-acre campus offers a serene and picturesque environment with exceptional facilities, providing the perfect balance of tranquillity and access to London and beyond.

Where your journey leads
From age 3 to 13, Feltonfleet nurtures happy, independent, resilient learners, with a strong sense of service, an abiding respect for others, and self confidence - a place where every pupil follows along their bespoke academic and personal pathway.
The Feltonfleet learning journey is broken into four stages, and culminates at Destination 13, when pupils leave Feltonfleet aged 13.

Admissions Process | Admissions | Feltonfleet School
Admissions
At Feltonfleet, we strive to make the admissions process as simple and welcoming as possible, tailored to meet your family's needs and timeline.
Whether you’re considering entry for Pre-School (3+), Reception (4+), Year 3 (7+), or Year 7 (11+), or exploring other entry points, we’re here to guide you every step of the way.
Our goal is to ensure the admissions process is as smooth and stress-free as possible, while helping you determine if Feltonfleet is the perfect fit for your child.
Director of Admissions | Alison Vernon
Step 1: Initial Enquiry
The first step is simply reaching out to us. You can do this by phone or email with our friendly Admissions Team. They’ll be your guides through the process, ensuring it’s customised to suit the needs of your child, with clear information for the specific year group you're interested in.
Step 2: Book a Visit
We believe that seeing Feltonfleet in person is the best way to understand what makes our school special. Whether you attend one of our Open Mornings or schedule a personalised visit (or both!), you’ll have the opportunity to meet our dedicated staff, interact with our wonderful pupils, and explore our beautiful campus. If visiting in person isn’t feasible, we also offer virtual meetings.
Step 3: Register your Child
Once you’ve decided Feltonfleet might be the right fit, the next step is to formally register your child. This process is handled online, and includes payment of a non-refundable registration fee. Registering your child allows us to keep you informed about the availability of places in your preferred year group and ensure you move forward in the admissions process when the time is right.
Step 4: Taster Visits
As your child’s potential start date approaches, they will be invited to a Taster Visit. For Prep School pupils, this typically involves spending a full day at Feltonfleet, paired with a buddy to help them settle in and experience a usual school day. Pre-Prep children will enjoy a shorter visit. During this time, children joining Year 3 or above will also participate in informal assessments in literacy, numeracy and reasoning, helping us tailor their learning journey should they join us.
Additionally, we will review your child’s latest school report and request a reference from their current school (if applicable) to ensure a smooth transition.
Our goal is to confirm that Feltonfleet is the right fit for your child academically and socially.
To ensure your child has the best chance of securing a place at Feltonfleet, we recommend arranging a Taster Visit in the Autumn Term of the year prior to entry. This is when the majority of places for the following September are allocated. While we aim to offer flexibility where possible, registering and scheduling a visit by September or October will maximise your child’s chances of being considered before places fill up, which often happens by Christmas.
If an in-person Taster Visit isn’t feasible, we will arrange a virtual meeting with your child to have a friendly chat, get to know them better, and provide an opportunity for them to learn more about Feltonfleet. For children joining Year 3 or above, we will also coordinate with their current school to facilitate the completion of our informal assessments in a familiar setting.
Step 5: Securing a Start Date
Following your child’s Taster Visit, we will contact you within two weeks to confirm the outcome. If a place is offered, you can secure it by accepting the offer, paying a refundable deposit and agreeing to our Terms & Conditions. At this stage, the start date will be confirmed, and we’ll eagerly prepare to welcome your child to Feltonfleet.
For those securing a place more than 12 months in advance, an acceptance deposit confirms the start date, subject to completing a Taster Visit closer to the time.
If you would like your child to be considered for a means-tested bursary, you may apply once your child has been offered a place in Year 3 or above. We strongly recommend that families interested in bursary support complete a preliminary application early in the admissions process. This will provide an initial assessment of your likelihood of success and help manage expectations.
Step 7: Preparing for Transition
In the Summer Term, we hold our Move Up Day, where pupils spend time with their new teachers and classmates, getting a taste of the excitement and opportunities in the upcoming academic year. Parents are also invited to induction events to meet the pastoral team and gain insights into the year ahead, making it a valuable and social occasion for both new and current families. Additionally, all new parents are warmly invited to a drinks reception with our Head, Shelley Lance, early in the Autumn Term.
For younger children joining our Early Years (Pre-School or Reception), we arrange home visits to help them transition smoothly, getting to know key people in their lives and sharing important information.

Anti-Bullying Culture
At Feltonfleet, our community is built on a foundation of respect, good manners, and fairness.
We are deeply committed to creating a safe and nurturing environment where every child can thrive without fear of disruption, harassment, or violence. Our goal is to ensure that all pupils can reach their full potential within a supportive and positive atmosphere.
The school sets clear expectations for how pupils behave towards each other, and how to look after younger students.
Parent of Year 7 Pupil
Central to our ethos is the expectation that pupils treat each other, and our staff, with courtesy and cooperation. We actively promote our core values of honesty, responsibility, respect, and kindness, and encourage pupils to care for and support one another.
We have a zero-tolerance policy towards bullying, harassment, victimisation, and discrimination. Any such behaviours are taken extremely seriously, and we ensure that all pupils and parents are treated with consideration and respect. At Feltonfleet, bullying in any form is simply unacceptable.
To foster an anti-bullying culture, we implement a range of preventative measures. These include comprehensive PSHE Education programmes, themed assemblies, and annual Anti-Bullying Workshops. Additionally, our Year 8 pupils, who hold positions of responsibility, act as mentors for younger students, offering guidance and support to any pupil who may have worries or concerns. Through these initiatives, we create a strong, supportive community where every child feels valued and secure.

Our Four Core Values | Pastoral Care | Feltonfleet School
Our Four Core Values
At Feltonfleet, our core values of honesty, responsibility, respect and kindness are the foundation of everything we do.
These principles aren’t just words on paper; they are the beliefs that help us to make decisions about how to behave. We believe that by living these values, our pupils develop into thoughtful, well-rounded individuals who contribute positively to the world around them.
I love how everyone feels part of the community and there is always someone to talk to.
Our school places a strong emphasis on recognising and rewarding positive behaviour, as we believe this fosters an ethos of kindness and cooperation - key ingredients for a thriving community. Rather than focusing solely on deterring anti-social behaviour, our approach to discipline is deeply rooted in Values education, the process by which people give moral values to each other. We actively promote and celebrate good behaviour as a way of nurturing a supportive, caring environment where every pupil feels valued and respected.
Here's how our core values come to life at Feltonfleet:
Pupils are encouraged to be truthful in their words and actions, fostering a culture of trust and integrity.
Pupils learn to be honest with themselves, recognising their strengths and areas for growth.
Honesty is also emphasised in their approach to learning—being honest about their efforts and progress.
Pupils are taught to take responsibility for their actions, recognising how their choices affect those around them.
We foster a strong sense of responsibility for learning, encouraging pupils to be accountable for their effort, progress, and behaviour in the classroom.
Responsibility also extends to the everyday - looking after personal belongings, respecting shared spaces, and caring for the property of others.
Respect starts with self-respect, which we encourage in every pupil.
We teach them to respect each other’s ideas, beliefs, and differences, fostering a community that values diversity and inclusivity.
Respect for the learning environment is also key, ensuring that everyone can thrive in a space that is supportive and conducive to growth.
Pupils are taught to be kind to themselves, practising mindfulness and self-care.
Kindness towards others is a daily expectation, from simple gestures to more significant acts of compassion.
We encourage random acts of kindness, reminding pupils that even small, unprompted actions can have a big impact on someone’s day.
These values permeate every aspect of life at Feltonfleet. They guide how we teach, how pupils learn, and how we interact with one another, ensuring that our school is not just a place of academic excellence but also a nurturing, compassionate community.
The school’s core values guide children on making decisions and good behaviour, equipping them for their future beyond Feltonfleet.

Pastoral Care | Feltonfleet School
Pastoral Care
At Feltonfleet, our core belief that every individual child really matters is the cornerstone of our pastoral care framework.
We are committed to ensuring that each pupil feels safe, supported, and valued. This commitment is embedded in every aspect of school life, with a robust pastoral system that prioritises the wellbeing and personal development of every student.
Pastoral care is taken seriously, with senior members of staff taking clear accountability. Incidents are rare, but are addressed promptly and head on.
Parent of Year 8 Pupil
Form Tutors play a central role in monitoring and nurturing their pupils' pastoral welfare, forming strong, trusting relationships with each child. They are supported by Heads and Deputy Heads of School, who oversee the pastoral care of pupils within their respective sections of the school - Pre-Prep, Lower, Middle, or Upper School - and by our Deputy Head (Pastoral), who brings particular expertise in child development and pastoral care.
Feltonfleet fosters an environment that promotes mindfulness and positive mental health. Wellbeing lessons are woven into the curriculum, providing pupils with dedicated time to relax, reflect, and build resilience. During Form Time, pupils have the opportunity to discuss their emotions and experiences with the support of their Form Tutors, reinforcing a school-wide ethos that encourages emotional expression and wellbeing.
For those who need additional support, our dedicated School Counsellor is available for drop-in sessions or scheduled appointments, offering pupils a safe space to work through challenges or boost their self-esteem. Pupils can self-refer or seek appointments through staff or parents, ensuring easy access to help when it's needed. Our on-site School Nurses are also on hand to provide first aid and reassurance, further enhancing the supportive environment.
Pupils tell us they feel known and seen.
Good Schools Guide 2024
To maintain a high standard of care, all staff undergo regular training in pastoral issues, ensuring they are well-equipped to address the needs of every pupil. We also offer information sessions for parents and pupils, covering key aspects of pastoral care and pupil welfare, reinforcing the strong partnership between school and home.
In the Prep School, pupils are encouraged to actively engage in discussions about pastoral issues, understanding their role in contributing to the wellbeing of the school community. Weekly PSHE Education lessons and participation in Pupil Voice Committees provide structured opportunities for reflection and dialogue, fostering a sense of responsibility and empathy among students.
Our culture of openness and approachability extends to parents, who are encouraged to reach out with any concerns, no matter how big or small. We believe in a close partnership between teachers and parents, working together to ensure the welfare and happiness of every pupil. All staff are easily contactable by email, reflecting our commitment to maintaining strong, transparent communication between home and school.

Learning Enrichment | Academic | Feltonfleet School
Learning Enrichment
Enrichment is at the heart of everything we do at Feltonfleet, and this ensures every child develops to their full potential, both academically and personally, whatever their needs or abilities.
Learning Enrichment is integral to our inclusive approach. When a pupil’s ability to learn, achieve or feel a sense of belonging is influenced by a learning difference or need, we take deliberate, adaptive action to support, challenge and nurture them within a caring environment.
We place great emphasis on understanding each pupil as an individual, recognising their unique background, family context and life experiences. Our commitment to inclusion means we actively ensure that all pupils, including those with special educational needs and disabilities, are visible, heard, represented and valued across the curriculum, within our resources, classroom environments and teaching practices.
Through our inclusive and supportive framework, every child is encouraged to reach their full potential, both academically and personally, whatever their starting point or individual needs.
Adaptive teaching is embedded in our school approach, enabling us to tailor learning to meet the diverse needs of our pupils. Through adaptive teaching methods, Learning Enrichment is integral to our teaching of all pupils, and all of our teachers take responsibility for its provision. Central to the work of every teacher is a continuous cycle of planning, teaching, assessment and evaluation that takes account of abilities, aptitudes and interests of the pupils.
At Feltonfleet, I feel accepted for who I am. Everyone is unique, and that diversity makes the world special. We all learn from each other and grow together.
Stretching Horizons
All pupils are challenged and encouraged to go beyond their comfort zone, to keep them engaged in the learning process and to see just what they can achieve. A wide range of extension and enrichment resources are used in lessons to stimulate pupils' interests and enhance their thinking skills. The goal is not to provide children who show mastery of a notion with ‘more of the same’ but is firmly on stimulating and challenging them to move beyond procedural knowledge to conceptual fluency, and to allow them to explore new ways of learning.
Additional Support
Early identification of learning barriers is essential to helping pupils succeed, which is why we regularly assess our current pupils and screen all new arrivals to create tailored learning support plans. Feltonfleet’s well-resourced Learning Enrichment department, centrally located within the school, is staffed by experienced and qualified teachers who specialise in supporting pupils with a range of specific learning difficulties, or who have English as a second language.
Our culture of acceptance, inclusion, and understanding helps all our pupils to embrace differences and champion each other's strengths. Learning Enrichment is part of every classroom - woven into every lesson - ensuring every pupil can thrive.
Head of Learning Enrichment | Fiona Houston
While the number of pupils with diagnosed special educational needs at Feltonfleet is relatively small, those pupils who do require additional support benefit from regular, specialist assistance, either individually, in a small group or in their regular class. We are committed to inclusivity,ensuring pupils with specific learning difficulties are fully integrated into our school community. They are valued members of our school, and we take great pride in the unique contributions they, and our Learning Enrichment department, make to our vibrant environment.

Bursaries
Each year, Feltonfleet allocates a limited amount of funds to our bursary scheme, aimed at providing access to a Feltonfleet education for pupils who might not otherwise have the opportunity.
These bursaries are reserved for children who would significantly benefit from our school's nurturing environment, such as:
When considering bursary applications, we carefully assess the extent of the family's financial need. Bursaries are awarded based on a thorough means-test that evaluates income, capital resources (such as the family home), and any existing debt. This process is repeated annually, ensuring that the support provided remains aligned with both financial need and the progress made by the recipient. All information is treated with the utmost confidentiality.
All children have the potential to thrive when given the right opportunities, and we believe it is both a privilege and a responsibility to offer those opportunities. In doing so, we not only transform the lives of the children we support, but also enrich the fabric of our entire school community.

Given the high demand for bursaries and the finite nature of our fund, not all deserving cases can be accommodated. We encourage families to apply only if they have a genuine financial need and for children who are likely to derive particular benefit. Bursaries are granted solely on this basis, and applications are only considered for children entering Year 3 or above.
Bursary applications are accepted throughout the academic year, but once the allocated funds are exhausted, no additional bursaries will be available until the following academic year, and only then if there are unallocated funds.
The school maintains full discretion over the allocation of bursaries and reserves the right to determine eligibility based on all relevant information.
